details.description: Secrets and API keys (PAYMENT_TOKEN, MAIL_SERVER_KEY, INTERNAL_AUTH) are hardcoded in the source making them retrievable from source control.
details.fix_explanation: Move all secrets and sensitive keys to environment variables and fail-safe logging. Read them using os.getenv and avoid embedding secrets directly in code.
details.secure_code_snippet:
PAYMENT_TOKEN = os.getenv("PAYMENT_TOKEN")
MAIL_SERVER_KEY = os.getenv("MAIL_SERVER_KEY")
INTERNAL_AUTH = os.getenv("INTERNAL_AUTH")

details.description: The SQL query is built using string interpolation with untrusted input which allows SQL injection attacks.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized SQL queries and validate input (e.g. allow only numeric IDs). This prevents user-supplied input from modifying the query structure.
details.secure_code_snippet: c.execute("SELECT id, name, balance FROM profiles WHERE id = ?", (uid,))

details.description: MD5 is a weak cryptographic hash and shouldn't be used for authentication tokens or secrets.
details.fix_explanation: Use HMAC with SHA256 and a server-side secret (INTERNAL_AUTH) to create secure tokens and avoid predictable hashes.
details.secure_code_snippet:
mac = hmac.new(INTERNAL_AUTH.encode(), username.encode(), hashlib.sha256)
return mac.hexdigest()

details.description: The notify_url parameter from input was used directly in requests.post allowing the server to be induced to reach attacker-specified URLs.
details.fix_explanation: Validate notify URLs strictly (https only and optional allowlist) before making outbound requests and use timeouts. Do not post to arbitrary client supplied endpoints.
details.secure_code_snippet:
if not _is_allowed_notify_url(notify_target): raise ValueError('notify_url is not allowed')
resp = requests.post(notify_target, json={ 'token': PAYMENT_TOKEN, 'amount': amt }, timeout=5)

details.description: The server read a path provided by the client directly which can disclose arbitrary files.
details.fix_explanation: Only allow loading configuration files from an approved directory, validate filename with os.path.basename, and disallow path traversal.

details.description: Calling subprocess with shell=True and untrusted input can lead to arbitrary command execution.
details.fix_explanation: Use Python stdlib (zipfile) to build archives instead of shelling out. Validate filename and avoid shell=True.
details.secure_code_snippet:
with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_name, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
    zf.write(DB_FILE, arcname=os.path.basename(DB_FILE))

details.description: Running Flask with debug=True enables the interactive debugger and code execution in production contexts.
details.fix_explanation: Disable debug mode and rely on proper deployment WSGI servers. Set debug=False and/or configure from environment.

details.vulnerability_type: Missing authentication / authorization for sensitive APIs
details.description: Critical operations (transfer, config load, export) performed without authentication allowing unauthorized access.
details.fix_explanation: Add authentication checks (e.g., header-based token verification or session validation) and ensure only authorized users can call sensitive operations.

details.description: Plain printing of transfer details can leak sensitive info to logs or console.
details.fix_explanation: Use the logging module with attention to not log sensitive data or redact values. Avoid prints in libraries/services.
details.secure_code_snippet: logger.info('processing transfer to target: %s (amount redacted)', target)
